extracted.intended_audience: privacy lawyers, compliance officers, in-house counsel, and businesses subject to California privacy law
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes the procedural steps, legal authorities, public-participation requirements, and timelines for California Privacy Protection Agency (CPPA) rulemaking regarding cybersecurity audits and risk assessments. Intended to guide stakeholders on how regulations are proposed, commented on, revised, and finalized under California law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Any rulemaking must be authorized by statute; authority for cybersecurity audits and risk assessment regulations derive from California Civil Code § 1798.185(a)(15)(A) and (B) and more broadly from the CCPA as amended by the CPRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All action by the CPPA must derive from legislative authority under the CCPA/CPRA; ensure proposed regulatory actions cite the enabling statute(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder input before formal rulemaking (preliminary comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before formal rulemaking commences, the CPPA invites preliminary comments and receives and processes public comments to inform drafting. The California Administrative Procedure Act requires this step 'to increase public participation and improve the quality of regulations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no statutory deadlines for this preliminary engagement; the CPPA generally seeks broad stakeholder engagement to ensure thorough consideration of new or amended rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft regulations and board discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: The CPPA releases draft regulations for board discussion and public participation; draft regulations often resemble the final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board meetings debate scope, applicability, timing, particulars of compliance (e.g., details required for audits and filings), and burdens on businesses — stakeholders should monitor board meetings for substantive changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Proposed Action and required materials
rubrics_metrics.description: To initiate formal rulemaking the CPPA must publish a 'notice of proposed action' in the California Regulatory Notice Register, post that notice to its website, and post 'express terms' (the text of the regulations) and an 'initial statement of reasons' explaining why the changes are proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice triggers formal comment periods and must include materials sufficient for stakeholders to understand the proposed rules and the agency's rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum 45-day public comment period
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice commences a period lasting a minimum of 45 days during which members of the public may submit comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CPPA is not required to hold a public hearing during this time unless requested by a member of the public, but it typically does hold hearings; the agency must respond to any oral comments made during a hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to summarize and respond to substantive comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The CPPA must summarize and respond to each substantive comment made by the public in response to the proposed regulations, accepting, accepting in part, or rejecting each one, and attach this dialogue in chart form as an appendix to a final statement of reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substantive comment is defined under California Government Code § 11346.9(2) as any 'objection or recommendation made regarding the specific adoption, amendment, or repeal proposed' and excludes mere support or background information. An index of commenters must accompany the chart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'substantive comment'
rubrics_metrics.description: A substantive comment includes any 'objection or recommendation made regarding the specific adoption, amendment, or repeal proposed,' according to California Government Code § 11346.9(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements that simply support the regulations or provide background information are not substantive comments for purposes of the CPPA's summary-and-response obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15-day supplemental comment periods for substantive modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Following initial review, if the CPPA substantively modifies the proposed regulations it must open a second comment period for a minimum of 15 days; if further changes are made in response to that period, another 15-day period must be opened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments received during each 15-day period must be summarized and responded to in the same manner as during the initial 45-day period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rulemaking package contents
rubrics_metrics.description: After processing comments, the CPPA must compile a final rulemaking package including: the text of the final regulations, any outside materials relied upon, a final statement of reasons with appended summaries/responses, and economic and fiscal impact statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all relied-upon materials are included and that the final statement of reasons documents how comments affected the final rule text.

rubrics_metrics.name: OAL review timeline and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Once submitted, the California Office of Administrative Law (OAL) has 30 working days to review the package for compliance with the California Administrative Procedure Act and OAL regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OAL may request communications to resolve minor issues but may disapprove the rulemaking for larger problems. If approved, OAL issues a 'notice of approval.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date mechanics and earliest-date request
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations come into effect on the OAL approval date, assuming the CPPA 'expressly requests' the earliest possible effective date and the OAL grants that request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must request the earliest effective date if they want immediate effect upon approval; prior judicial decisions may alter the practical effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12-month effective-date delay stemming from court decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the Sacramento County Superior Court decision, the effective date of pending CPPA rules will be 12 months from the date of finalization; the court determined a 12-month period aligns with voter intent to give affected businesses time to comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if OAL approval occurs, stakeholders should plan for a 12-month compliance window for future rules unless the court landscape changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cybersecurity audit requirement (as drafted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once finalized, businesses will be required to perform annual independent cybersecurity audits to assess, document and summarize the components of their cybersecurity programs, focusing on any gaps or weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft regulations enumerate examples of 'negative impacts' on consumers' security and require assessment of safeguards businesses use to protect personal information; businesses should prepare to engage independent auditors and document remediation plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk assessment triggers (examples of activities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk assessments must be conducted and submitted whenever a business's personal information processing presents a significant risk to consumers' privacy or security; the draft regulations provide seven examples, including 'selling or sharing personal information,' 'processing sensitive personal information,' and 'processing the personal information of consumers' to train AI or automated decision-making technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders should map processing activities to the listed examples to determine whether an assessment is required and consider edge cases such as AI training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk assessment required components
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk assessments would be comprised of 10 components, including a summary of the processing, categories of personal information to be processed, operational elements of the processing, purposes of the processing, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare templates that capture the required components (e.g., processing summary, data categories, operational details, purposes) so assessments can be completed consistently and submitted when triggered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and litigation value of comment processing
rubrics_metrics.description: The CPPA's obligation to summarize/respond to comments creates a substantial paper record within which public concerns are given due consideration, and the CPPA's official positions on particulars of the regulations are developed with meticulous detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final statement of reasons and appendices can provide useful authority in litigation challenging the regulations; stakeholders should carefully document comments and the agency's responses to support legal arguments or administrative advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical timeline benchmarking from prior CPRA rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Past timeline: invitation for public comment predating CPRA regulations was approved 29 March and first published 564 days prior; the formal rulemaking process from notice register publication to OAL approval lasted 244 days; accounting for a 12-month delay, the prior round would have taken until ~Aug. 2025 to come into effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These historical benchmarks can help stakeholders estimate plausible timelines for current rulemaking, but scope differences mean timing may vary.
